item.title: Advanced manufacturing, green energy, digital tech drive rise of exports
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Technological industrialization and the leapfrogging development of emerging technologies are creating new opportunities for the globalization of Chinese companies, said experts and top executives. Chinese companies' rising global competitiveness in advanced manufacturing, green energy and digital technology, and high-tech products has become a key driver of export growth. Export value surged 39 percent year-on-year to 3.26 trillion yuan ($490 billion) in the first half of 2026, according to professional services provider Deloitte. With artificial intelligence's deeper integration into industries, the intelligent transformation in advanced manufacturing and technology is accelerating, promoting China's technology-intensive industries worldwide, according to the report jointly compiled by Deloitte, the Yicai Research Institute and media service provider Chin@Moment. The competitiveness of Chinese companies is no longer confined to one single product. It is about their strengths in the global industrial chain, which is reflected by the rising global status of Chinese companies specializing in advanced equipment, digital economy, photovoltaic technology, energy storage and other sectors, said Zhou Hanmin, chairman of the Shanghai Public Diplomacy Association. China's new energy industry is expected to play a bigger role in overseas energy transition. Growing AI investment has driven up electricity demand globally. This has been translated into higher requirements for flexible power systems, energy security, energy storage, and energy management technologies, all of which coincide with Chinese companies' competitive edges, according to the report released during the ninth China International Import Expo, which was concluded on Nov 10 in Shanghai. These companies need to build global management capabilities in market entry regulations, local distribution channels, tax and compliance to become international industry leaders, said Zhou. China's overseas direct investment hit a record $213.58 billion in 2025, accounting for 11.5 percent of the global total. Outbound investment stock reached $3.38 trillion, ranking among the world's top three for the ninth consecutive year. This marks an acceleration in Chinese companies' "going global" pace and their growing ability to build a global presence, the report said. The globalization of Chinese companies is taking multiple forms. Overseas mergers and acquisitions, greenfield investment, and local production have become mainstream paths for companies to get closer to target markets. New models are also emerging, such as technology licensing and cooperation, said the report. Lydia Chen, Deloitte China Research Managing Partner, said the globalization of Chinese companies has moved beyond the phase of simply exporting products. Integrating into the local industrial ecosystem will define their success in the overseas expansion, she said. Precision medical laser equipment provider Shanghai Raykeen Laser Technology is recognized by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology as a "little giant" manufacturing company. In its 13-year history, the company has sold its products in more than 20 overseas markets. The company's general manager, Zhang Jingshen, said establishing industry standards was one of their major ways of expanding into new markets. China's technologies and training systems are quite advanced in certain areas, she said. Exporting these innovations can lead to regulated development of the local markets and also explains the popularity of Chinese products, Zhang said. Lawrence Jin, chief growth officer for Deloitte China, said outbound Chinese companies should strike a balance between long-term strategy and agile operation, compliance and commercial efficiency, and global management and local adaptation. Xu Heng, general manager for cross-border business at the president's office of food and beverage company Tingyi Holding, said in-depth analysis of target markets, a local team and active participation in international exhibitions are crucial factors for Chinese brands aiming to go global. The success of Chinese retail brands such as Pop Mart and Chinese gaming companies has shown the appeal of Chinese culture. Retailers can also leverage short dramas to better build their brand names by adding more Chinese cultural elements, she said. According to Qin Shuo, founder of Chin@Moment and a veteran financial commentator, the global expansion of Chinese companies is now balanced like a dumbbell, with low-end products and high-end products both seeing strong export momentum. On one hand, overseas expansion is crucial to Chinese companies' evolution. On the other, Chinese companies are needed to fill the gaps in other markets in terms of infrastructure, smart manufacturing, digitalization and e-retailing, said Qin. "As experts from the World Economic Forum wrote in a paper last year, China's structural advantage in integrating innovation and manufacturing may prove to be the most lasting hidden wealth of the country, exemplified by the mobile phone supply chain strength extended to new energy vehicles, drones and smart energy," he said. "Against that backdrop, Chinese companies should stick to the rule of creating value for consumers and all stakeholders to ensure their sustainable development in overseas markets." shijing@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: APEC media center opens, offers reporters tech tools
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
The media center for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week opened on Wednesday, offering nearly 5,000 Chinese and foreign journalists reporting facilities, artificial intelligence-powered production tools and cultural experiences. Set up at the Shenzhen Convention and Exhibition Center in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, the facility is spread over 15,000 square meters and is divided into functional zones, providing services such as free internet access, media workstations and technical support for reporters covering the meetings. It also features news conference halls and an international broadcasting center. The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting is scheduled for Nov 18 and 19 in the southern Chinese tech hub. A key feature of the media center is its digital intelligence integration. It is home to the nation's first Harmony-OS smart studio, which is equipped with XR, or extended reality, virtual recording technology and 4K ultrahigh-definition signal transmission capabilities. Intelligent editing tools are also available to help journalists quickly edit and produce content in multiple languages, significantly enhancing publication efficiency. Technology has also been integrated into hospitality services. At the Journalists' Home, robots prepare coffee and serve ice cream, while delivery robots bring drinks and snacks. During the APEC Economic Leaders' Week, which will be held from Friday to Nov 19 in Shenzhen, the media center will host a variety of events, including official news briefings and city tours. chenhong@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Authentic villages where heritage thrives
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
For Kyle Obermann, an environmental photographer from the United States, Zhejiang province's Songyang county redefined what hiking in China meant for him. "Hiking through the ancient villages of the county was wonderfully cathartic and rejuvenating. I loved the old camphor trees that many of the villages have nurtured and lived under for centuries," he said. There, he saw an entirely different side of China — a slow life grounded in tradition. "The well-preserved and restored traditional earthen and wooden architecture of the homes was a welcome and healing sight after spending too much time in New York or other big cities of the world," he added. Songyang's history as an administrative division goes back some 1,800 years. Seventy-eight traditional villages survive there, many retaining their original layouts, ancestral halls, bridges and earthen homes. For travelers, this experience offers something rare in China. Villages feel genuinely inhabited, rather than being heavily commercialized attractions built specifically for tourists. For Wu Xi, a 38-year-old from Shanghai, quietness is the attraction. About a month ago, Wu visited Pingtian and Xikeng villages of Songyang with his mother, having already seen the better-known Chenjiapu and Yangjiatang villages on earlier trips. In Pingtian, he found a village with an artistic atmosphere: old houses had been turned into calligraphy exhibition spaces featuring local artists. "I saw only about 10 tourists in the entire village," he said. The village is halfway up a hillside, where elderly residents sit by their doors and chat. "I prefer less-developed places," he added. Yangjiatang, however, left the strongest impression. Wu visited the village last year with friends and ate at a Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) farmhouse complete with wooden partitions, dim old lamps and a small courtyard. "It felt like a home from the 1980s or 1990s — but clean and tidy," he said. There was no menu. They simply asked for what they wanted, ordering dishes such as chili stir-fried pork. "It didn't feel like a restaurant. It felt like eating in a local family's home, like going back to childhood." Built around 1655, Yangjiatang is one of the most dramatic villages. Dozens of Qing Dynasty houses climb the slope in uneven tiers, asymmetrical yet harmonious. At dusk, the last glimmers of sunlight turn the rammed-earth walls to a deep golden hue, making the entire hillside village glow for moments. What keeps Songyang's villages authentic is that people still live and work in them. That approach is something Wu Haiyan, director of the county's bureau of culture, radio, television, tourism and sports, put simply: "What we are trying to build is a Songyang where people can find an ideal way of life and still see the nostalgic image of the China they remember." The villages also have their own distinct characteristics. Chenjiapu offers striking natural views. Perched on a cliffside, the village offers views of clouds drifting through the valley below. Yangjiatang, meanwhile, has a richer cultural heritage and more concentrated and intact clusters of old buildings, requiring a more cautious approach to preservation. Youtian serves as a cultural hub. It features a global translator residency program, bringing translators and cultural figures to give lectures and hold discussions at the village hall. Some of the villages can be visited consecutively by car in a day. Many guesthouses are converted century-old earthen houses, which are authentic outside and comfortable inside.

item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING -- President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925. Thursday's gathering in the Great Hall of the People was attended by about 3,000 people, including senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. Wang presided over the event. Xi met with Sun's relatives and representatives of overseas guests before the event started. In his speech, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution. He said that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said. "The best way for us to remember Dr Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said. Highlighting Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, Xi called on all Chinese people to learn from Sun and promote patriotism to strive for a strong and prosperous China. He also lauded Sun's dedication to the people, underscoring the imperative of always putting the people first and serving them wholeheartedly. On the new journey, it is essential to make solid headway in promoting well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all, Xi stressed. Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. Xi called on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development. "We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said. Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Highlighting Sun's global vision, Xi called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. "Dr Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation," Xi said. Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said. "On the basis of adhering to the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, we are willing to engage in dialogue and consultations with people of vision and insight from all sectors in Taiwan on matters related to cross-Strait relations and national reunification," Xi said. "We will definitely give full consideration to Taiwan's realities and take full account of the interests and feelings of our compatriots in Taiwan," Xi said. "But we will never leave any room for 'Taiwan independence' separatist activities in any form." "The historical trends are unstoppable. The complete reunification of our motherland must be realized, and it can, without doubt, be realized," Xi said.

item.title: Yunnan turns tea into tourist trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
On the slopes of Pu'er's Jingmai Mountain, tea comes in more than just a steaming cup. In Nuogan village, Dai ethnic entrepreneur Xianjin sells her signature Pu'er tea in an ice cream cone. Nearby, a Blang ethnic tea grower and a Dai businessman have joined forces, serving each other's traditional tea under one roof. The bustling mountain trade was supercharged three years ago after UNESCO added the Cultural Landscape of Old Tea Forests of Jingmai Mountain in Pu'er to its World Heritage List. On Sept 17, 2023, when the announcement was made, entrepreneur Xianjin watched her modest online tea business transform overnight. Earlier that day, her livestreams generated barely 700 yuan ($100). By midnight, as viewers flooded her channel to buy a piece of the world's newest heritage site, sales topped 130,000 yuan. Her experience reflects a massive economic shift underway in Southwest China's Yunnan province, as Jingmai Mountain's 1,000-year-old agroforestry system turns into a major tourism driver. Local government figures show the area recorded 694,300 tourist visits and 563 million yuan in tourism revenue in 2025, nearly doubling average annual incomes for tea-related residents from 15,410 yuan before the listing to about 26,000 yuan afterward. Yet, this influx of visitors presents a delicate challenge: sustaining an ecosystem built on centuries of minimal human impact while capitalizing on a lucrative commercial boom.

item.title: Rapid global growth a trove of opportunity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
The fast-evolving Chinese market and active overseas expansion of Chinese companies are consistently offering tremendous opportunities for global services providers, business leaders said during the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai. Having participated in the expo for all nine of its editions, Marriott International has seen rapid growth in the Chinese market, driven by the nation's robust travel sector. As of the end of September, the company had opened more than 100 new hotels in China this year, up more than 30 percent year-on-year with an average of 2.6 hotels opening each week. By the end of November, it will reach another milestone with the opening of its 800th hotel in China. Mao Yibing, president of Marriott International Greater China, said China continues to advance high-level opening-up, and its tourism consumption remains robust.

item.title: Rice-prawn technology from China lifts Cambodian aquaculture
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
In Takeo province, Cambodia, farmers are growing rice and raising giant freshwater prawns in the same fields, with support from a team led by Professor Wu Xugan of Shanghai Ocean University. This "one field, two harvests" model has doubled local farmers' incomes and been recognized by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations as one of the best practices for poverty reduction. Follow China Daily reporter Owen Fishwick to see how Chinese experts are helping Cambodian farmers boost their incomes.

item.title: PLA Air Force marks 77th anniversary amid modernization drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING -- The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force marked its 77th founding anniversary on Wednesday, highlighting its journey from a modest beginning to a modernizing force with a structure geared toward future operational needs. In an anniversary video, the Air Force, founded on Nov 11, 1949, showcased training exercises involving fighter jets, bombers, early warning aircraft, transport planes, helicopters and drones, as well as ground-based air defense missile units, radar units and airborne troops. The video, released Wednesday on the service's official social media accounts, also highlighted the Air Force's participation in disaster relief and international exchanges, drawing a wave of congratulatory messages. Anniversary celebrations had begun earlier this month, with events held in different parts of the country. On Monday morning, eight flight instructors from the Aviation University of the Air Force in Changchun, capital of Northeast China's Jilin province, took to the skies in jet trainers for an aerial display. That evening, 3,000 drones lit up the sky in a light show depicting the Air Force's evolution, from horse-towed propeller-driven trainer aircraft, to advanced aircraft such as J-20 stealth fighter and Y-20 transport plane. On Nov 6, six J-10 jets from the PLA Air Force's Bayi (August 1) Aerobatic Team flew over the Great Wall in North China's Tianjin municipality as part of the celebrations. The team derives its name from the founding anniversary of the PLA. "The Great Wall was once a barrier against invaders," said Zha Xiufeng, one of the pilots. "Today, we pilots serve as an 'airborne Great Wall,' safeguarding the peace and security of countless families." The PLA Air Force started with a small fleet of outdated aircraft. During the founding ceremony of the People's Republic of China on Oct 1, 1949, only 17 aircraft were available for parade. In the following years, the Air Force shot down or damaged more than 3,800 enemy aircraft, according to official figures. More than 1,800 Air Force personnel have given their lives in combat operations, scientific research tasks, and dedication to the interests of the people. The PLA Air Force's three-step development roadmap, issued in 2018, set targets to build a strategic air force by 2020, basically establish a modernized strategic air force by 2035, and become a world-class air force by the middle of the century. The 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, scheduled to run from Dec 7 to 13 in Zhuhai, will offer the world a glimpse of the PLA Air Force's latest developments. The Air Force said multiple types of its main combat equipment would make their debut at the show. Equipment for aerial reconnaissance, early warning, air defense, support, airborne operations, unmanned applications and intelligent systems, as well as munitions, will also be displayed at the exhibition. "Bringing more domestically developed new-generation aircraft closer to the public and taking Air Force stories into households across the country are commitments we will continue to uphold," said Gao Xiang, a senior Air Force official. As the PLA Air Force has developed, its international engagement has also expanded. In 2026, the Bayi Aerobatic Team performed at the 10th Singapore Airshow, while a range of aircraft, including fighters, tankers, special-purpose aircraft and helicopters, took part in the China-Egypt "Eagles of Civilization 2026" joint air force training as an integrated force. Moreover, Chinese and Russian air forces conducted a joint strategic patrol over the western Pacific and other airspace, demonstrating their resolve and capability to uphold regional peace and stability. Chinese and Belarusian airborne troops also held urban counterterrorism exercises in Central China. "We will continue to engage with our counterparts around the world, build mutual trust through interaction, deepen cooperation through exchanges, and work together to safeguard the shared airspace of humanity," Gao said.
